Lemma
[Monotonicity of $R_{\min }(t)$ (Lemma 32.3)] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iv:page-0224 1. ch32:32.3\group Scalar Curvature Cases

Let $(\mathcal M^n,g(t))$ be a normalized Ricci flow on a closed manifold.

  1. If $R_{\min }(t_0)>0$, then $R_{\min }(t)>0$ for every $t\ge t_0$.

  2. If $R_{\min }(t)\le 0$ for all $t$, then $R_{\min }$ is nondecreasing. If in addition the flow is not Einstein, then it is strictly increasing.

Proof

\sketch While $R_{\min }>0$, (32.4) gives

\[ \frac d{dt}\log R_{\min } \ge \frac2n(R_{\min }-r)>-\frac2n r. \]

Since $r$ is bounded on every compact time interval, a positive minimum cannot reach zero in finite time. If $R_{\min }\le 0$, then $R_{\min }-r\le 0$, so the right-hand side of (32.4) is nonnegative. If equality occurs at two distinct times, monotonicity makes $R_{\min }$ constant between them. The strong maximum principle applied to (32.3) then makes $R$ spatially constant and forces equality in $|\Rc |^2\ge R^2/n$; hence $g(t)$ is Einstein. Thus a non-Einstein flow has strictly increasing $R_{\min }$.

□
